name: iOS Development
description: Native iOS apps with Swift and SwiftUI, data and networking, platform features and App Store release.

nodes.name: Swift basics
nodes.desc: Constants, variables, control flow, functions, closures and collections.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write basic Swift code with constants, variables, control flow, functions, closures and the standard collection types.
topics: let vs var and type inference
Control flow with if, switch and loops

nodes.name: Swift type system
nodes.desc: Structs, classes, enums, optionals and value versus reference semantics.
nodes.summary: You will understand Swift's type system well enough to choose between structs, classes and enums and handle optionals safely.

nodes.name: Protocols & generics
nodes.desc: Protocol-oriented design, extensions and generic code.
nodes.summary: You will be able to design protocol-oriented Swift code using protocols, extensions and generics with constraints.

nodes.name: Swift concurrency
nodes.desc: async/await, tasks, actors and the main actor.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write safe asynchronous Swift code with async/await, tasks and actors and keep UI work on the main actor.

nodes.name: Xcode
nodes.desc: Projects, targets, simulators, previews and the debugger.
nodes.summary: You will be able to navigate Xcode projects and targets, run apps in simulators, use SwiftUI previews and debug with breakpoints.

nodes.name: SwiftUI views
nodes.desc: Views, modifiers and composing interfaces.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build interfaces in SwiftUI by composing small views and applying modifiers in the right order.

nodes.name: State & bindings
nodes.desc: @State, @Binding and how SwiftUI updates views.
nodes.summary: You will understand how SwiftUI re-renders views when state changes and be able to share state between views with bindings.

nodes.name: Lists & navigation
nodes.desc: Lists, NavigationStack and sheets.
nodes.summary: You will be able to display data in lists and move between screens with NavigationStack, navigation links and sheets.
topics: List and ForEach with identifiable data

nodes.name: Layout & modifiers
nodes.desc: Stacks, grids, spacing, adaptive layout and styling.
nodes.summary: You will be able to lay out SwiftUI screens with stacks and grids that adapt to different sizes and apply consistent styling.

nodes.name: First SwiftUI app
nodes.desc: Build a multi-screen SwiftUI app with lists and navigation.
nodes.summary: You will build a multi-screen SwiftUI app that shows data in lists and navigates between detail and edit screens.

nodes.name: Observable & MVVM
nodes.desc: The Observation framework, view models and app architecture.
nodes.summary: You will be able to structure a SwiftUI app with the Observation framework and view models following the MVVM pattern.

nodes.name: SwiftData
nodes.desc: Persisting models, queries and relationships with SwiftData.
nodes.summary: You will be able to persist app data with SwiftData models, fetch it with queries and model relationships between objects.

nodes.name: URLSession & Codable
nodes.desc: Fetching JSON with URLSession and decoding it with Codable.
nodes.summary: You will be able to fetch JSON from web APIs with URLSession and decode it into Swift types with Codable.
topics: Handling HTTP errors and status codes

nodes.name: UIKit basics
nodes.desc: UIKit view controllers and bridging UIKit and SwiftUI.
nodes.summary: You will understand UIKit's view controller model and be able to embed UIKit views in SwiftUI and SwiftUI views in UIKit.

nodes.name: Journal app
nodes.desc: Build a journal app with local storage and data from a web API.
nodes.summary: You will build a journal app that stores entries locally and enriches them with data fetched from a web API.

nodes.name: Privacy & permissions
nodes.desc: Permission prompts, privacy manifests and camera, photos and location.
nodes.summary: You will be able to request camera, photos and location access correctly and declare data use in privacy manifests.

nodes.name: Background tasks
nodes.desc: Background refresh, processing tasks and app lifecycle.
nodes.summary: You will understand the iOS app lifecycle and be able to schedule background refresh and processing tasks within system limits.

nodes.name: Notifications
nodes.desc: Local and push notifications.
nodes.summary: You will be able to schedule local notifications and understand how push notifications are delivered through APNs.

nodes.name: Widgets & extensions
nodes.desc: Home screen widgets and app extensions sharing data.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build Home Screen widgets with WidgetKit and share data between an app and its extensions.

nodes.name: Testing iOS apps
nodes.desc: Unit tests, UI tests and testing async code.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write unit and UI tests for iOS apps and test asynchronous code reliably.
topics: Unit tests with XCTest or Swift Testing

nodes.name: Instruments
nodes.desc: Profiling time, memory and energy with Instruments.
nodes.summary: You will be able to profile an app with Instruments to find slow code, memory leaks and excessive energy use.

nodes.name: App Store release
nodes.desc: Signing, TestFlight, App Store Connect and review guidelines.
nodes.summary: You will be able to sign, distribute through TestFlight and submit an app to the App Store in line with review guidelines.

nodes.name: iOS capstone
nodes.desc: Ship a polished app with persistence, notifications and a widget through TestFlight.
nodes.summary: You will ship a polished iOS app with persistence, notifications and a widget and distribute it to testers via TestFlight.
